summary: 想, 要, 想要, 愿意, 得 (děi), 应该 and 打算 all sit before a verb and say how much you want, intend or have to do it. Think of a scale: 想 is a wish (would like to), 要 is a decision or a necessity (want, going to, have to), 得 is pure obligation. The negatives do not mirror the positives: 不想 = don't feel like, 不要 = don't!, 不用 = no need to.

subs.label: 想 + verb: would like to
subs.focus: Choose 想 + verb for a soft wish ('would like to, feel like'); negative 不想. Mistakes: 想 + noun meant as 'want' (我想咖啡); 要 after 很/非常/有点儿 (only 想 takes a degree adverb). Include a cue (degree adverb, 可是没时间, 'feel like') that excludes 要.

subs.label: 想 = think / miss
subs.focus: Read 想 by what follows: person/place = miss, clause = think, 想一下/想想/想办法 = think over. Mistakes: 要 for 'miss'; reading 我想你 as 'I want you'; negating an opinion as 我不想他会来 instead of 我觉得他不会来.

subs.label: 要 + noun: want, ordering; 要 + verb: firm want
subs.focus: Choose 要 when a thing is wanted or ordered (noun follows, usually number + measure) or the want is a firm decision (一定要). Mistakes: 我想一杯咖啡 when ordering; 很要; soft 想 where the context shows insistence. In ordering items put a noun right after the blank.

subs.label: 要 = going to / need to / takes (time, money)
subs.focus: Recognise 要 as 'going to' (time word or 了), 'need to / must', and 'takes / costs' before a duration or amount. Mistakes: negating 'going to' with 不要 (我明天不要去) instead of 不 / 不会 / 不打算; using 想 for a fixed plan or for how long something takes.

subs.label: 不想 / 不要 / 不用
subs.focus: Pick 不想 (don't feel like), 不要 / 别 (don't!, a command) or 不用 (no need to). Mistakes: 你不要来 meant as 'you needn't come'; answering 要...吗 ('need to?') with 不要 instead of 不用. Each item needs a cue (reason clause, 我自己可以, 危险) forcing exactly one.

subs.label: 得 (děi) must, negative 不用
subs.focus: Use 得 (děi) + verb for 'have to'; its negative is 不用 and it has no 得不得 question. Mistakes: 不得去 for 'don't have to go'; 得不得去; 得 placed after the verb or before the time word. May also contrast 得 (no choice) with 想 (wish).

subs.label: 想要 + noun / verb
subs.focus: Use 想要 for 'would like to have' + noun (or + verb); negative 不想要. Choose it over bare 想 when a noun follows and over bare 要 when 很 / 非常 is present. Mistakes: 我想一个新手机; 很要一个新手机; 不要想 for 不想要.

subs.label: 愿意: willing
subs.focus: Choose 愿意 + verb when the point is consent or willingness (often something asked of you), not desire; negative 不愿意, question 愿不愿意 / 愿意...吗. Mistakes: 想 or 要 for 'willing'; 愿意 + noun (我愿意咖啡); 愿意 for a simple wish like wanting tea.

subs.label: 应该 should / 打算 plan to
subs.focus: Choose 应该 for advice, duty or expectation (weaker than 得 / 要) and 打算 for a considered plan (vs 想 a wish). Mistakes: 不用 where 不应该 'shouldn't' is meant; 想 with a firm-plan cue; time word after the verb (我打算去明年).

rules.rule: 想 + verb means 'would like to, feel like'. It is a wish, not a decision, so it can take 很, 非常, 有点儿, and its negative is 不想. To want a thing, add a verb or use 要 / 想要.

examples.py: wǒ xiǎng hē bēi chá
examples.en: I'd like a cup of tea.

examples.py: wǒ hěn xiǎng qù běi jīng kàn kan
examples.en: I'd really like to go and see Beijing.

examples.zh: 今天太累了，我不想做饭。
examples.py: jīn tiān tài lèi le wǒ bù xiǎng zuò fàn
examples.en: I'm too tired today; I don't feel like cooking.

rules.note: 想 and 要 both translate 'want to' and often either is possible; 想 is softer and more polite, 要 sounds decided. Only 想 accepts 很 / 非常.

rules.rule: 想 + person or place = miss. 想 + a clause = think (an opinion or guess). 想想, 想一下, 想办法 = think something over. Put the negative inside the clause, or use 觉得.
rules.pattern: Subject + 想 + person  |  Subject + 想 + clause  |  Subject + 想 + 一下

examples.py: wǒ hěn xiǎng wǒ mā ma
examples.en: I miss my mum a lot.

examples.py: wǒ xiǎng tā jīn tiān bù huì lái le
examples.en: I don't think he's coming today.

examples.py: ràng wǒ xiǎng yī xià zài gào su nǐ
examples.en: Let me think about it and then tell you.

examples.py: nǐ xiǎng jiā ma
examples.en: Are you homesick?

rules.note: 我想你 normally means 'I miss you'. For 'think about / of' a topic, Chinese usually says 想 + what is being considered (我在想明天的考试) rather than a bare person.

rules.rule: 要 takes a noun directly: 'I want / I'll have'. This is the normal way to order or buy. Before a verb, 要 is a firm want: you have decided. 要 never takes 很.
rules.pattern: Subject + 要 + number + measure + Noun  |  Subject + (一定) + 要 + Verb

examples.py: wǒ yào yī bēi kā fēi
examples.en: I'll have a coffee.

examples.py: nǐ yào shén me
examples.en: What would you like?

examples.py: wǒ yī dìng yào xué hǎo zhōng wén
examples.en: I'm determined to learn Chinese well.

examples.py: zhè ge wǒ bù yào le xiè xie
examples.en: I don't want this one any more, thanks.

rules.note: With a noun, 不要 simply means 'don't want (it)' and is not rude or a command.

rules.rule: 要 + verb with a time word or 了 means 'going to'. In other contexts it means 'need to, have to'. Negate 'going to' with 不 / 不会 / 不打算, not 不要.
rules.pattern: Subject + time + 要 + Verb  |  (快)要 + Verb + 了

examples.py: wǒ míng tiān yào qù shàng hǎi chū chāi
examples.en: I'm going to Shanghai on business tomorrow.

examples.py: yào xià yǔ le kuài huí jiā ba
examples.en: It's about to rain; hurry home.

examples.py: guò mǎ lù de shí hou yào xiǎo xīn
examples.en: You need to be careful when crossing the road.

examples.py: wǒ míng tiān bù qù shàng hǎi le
examples.en: I'm not going to Shanghai tomorrow after all.

rules.note: Whether 要 means 'want to', 'going to' or 'have to' comes from context; many real sentences allow two readings. Drill items need a cue that fixes one.

rules.rule: 要 before a duration or an amount means 'takes, costs, needs'.
rules.pattern: (从 A 到 B / Verb phrase) + 要 + duration / amount

examples.py: zuò huǒ chē qù yào liǎng gè xiǎo shí
examples.en: It takes two hours to go by train.

examples.py: zhè jiàn yī fu yào sān bǎi kuài
examples.en: This piece of clothing costs three hundred yuan.

examples.zh: 从这儿到机场要多长时间？
examples.py: cóng zhè r dào jī chǎng yào duō cháng shí jiān
examples.en: How long does it take to get from here to the airport?

rules.note: 需要 also works here and sounds a little more formal. The negative is 不用 or 用不了: 不用两个小时 'it doesn't take two hours'.

rules.rule: Three different negatives: 不想 + verb = don't feel like it (my wish). 不要 + verb, said to someone = don't! (same as 别). 不用 + verb = no need to (the negative of 要 / 得 'must').
rules.pattern: 不想 + Verb (no wish)  |  (你) + 不要 / 别 + Verb (command)  |  不用 + Verb (no need)

examples.zh: 我不想去，我想在家休息。
examples.py: wǒ bù xiǎng qù wǒ xiǎng zài jiā xiū xi
examples.en: I don't want to go; I'd like to rest at home.

examples.zh: 上课的时候不要玩手机。
examples.py: shàng kè de shí hou bù yào wán shǒu jī
examples.en: Don't play on your phone in class.

examples.zh: 你不用来接我，我自己坐地铁。
examples.py: nǐ bù yòng lái jiē wǒ wǒ zì jǐ zuò dì tiě
examples.en: You don't need to pick me up; I'll take the metro myself.

examples.py: míng tiān yào zǎo qǐ ma bù yòng
examples.en: Do we have to get up early tomorrow? No, no need.

rules.note: 我不要去 does occur, but as a strong refusal ('I won't go!'), common from children and in southern speech. For an ordinary 'I don't want to go', say 我不想去.

rules.rule: 得, read děi, + verb means 'have to, must': circumstances force it. It is colloquial, has no 不得 negative and no 得不得 question. 'Don't have to' is 不用.
rules.pattern: Subject + (time) + 得 + Verb  →  negative: Subject + 不用 + Verb

examples.py: tài wǎn le wǒ děi zǒu le
examples.en: It's late; I have to go.

examples.zh: 明天有考试，今天晚上我得复习。
examples.py: míng tiān yǒu kǎo shì jīn tiān wǎn shang wǒ děi fù xí
examples.en: There's an exam tomorrow, so I have to revise tonight.

examples.zh: 明天是星期六，你不用上班。
examples.py: míng tiān shì xīng qī liù nǐ bù yòng shàng bān
examples.en: Tomorrow is Saturday; you don't have to go to work.

rules.note: 得 (děi) and 要 'must' are close; 得 is more spoken and stresses that there is no choice. 得 can also be followed by a duration or amount: 得两个小时 'it'll take a good two hours'. Do not confuse it with 得 de after a verb (跑得快) or 不得 bù dé in formal 'must not' notices.

rules.rule: 想要 = 'would like to have / would like to'. It takes a noun (which bare 想 cannot, in this meaning) or a verb, and it accepts 很. Negative: 不想要.
rules.pattern: Subject + (很) + 想要 + Noun  |  Subject + 想要 + Verb

examples.py: wǒ xiǎng yào yī gè xīn shǒu jī
examples.en: I'd like a new phone.

examples.py: nǐ shēng rì xiǎng yào shén me lǐ wù
examples.en: What present would you like for your birthday?

examples.py: tā hěn xiǎng yào yī zhī xiǎo gǒu
examples.en: She really wants a puppy.

examples.py: zhè zhǒng yán sè wǒ bù xiǎng yào
examples.en: I don't want this colour.

rules.note: Before a verb, 想要 and 想 are usually interchangeable (我想要学开车 = 我想学开车); 想 alone is more common in speech. When ordering food or drink, plain 要 or 来 is what people say.

rules.rule: 愿意 + verb = 'be willing to': you agree to do it, whether or not you desire it. Negative 不愿意; question 愿意...吗 or 愿不愿意. It is followed by a verb, not a noun.
rules.pattern: Subject + (不 / 很) + 愿意 + Verb

examples.py: nǐ yuàn yì bāng wǒ yī gè máng ma
examples.en: Are you willing to do me a favour?

examples.zh: 他不愿意搬到别的城市去。
examples.py: tā bù yuàn yì bān dào bié de chéng shì qù
examples.en: He isn't willing to move to another city.

examples.zh: 只要工资高，我愿意加班。
examples.py: zhǐ yào gōng zī gāo wǒ yuàn yì jiā bān
examples.en: As long as the pay is good, I'm willing to work overtime.

rules.note: 不愿意 is stronger and more principled than 不想: 不想去 = don't feel like going; 不愿意去 = unwilling to go, even if asked.

rules.rule: 应该 + verb = 'should, ought to' (advice or duty, weaker than 得 / 要); it can also mean 'should be, probably'. Negative: 不应该 = 'should not', which is not the same as 不用 'need not'.

examples.py: nǐ gǎn mào le yīng gāi duō hē shuǐ
examples.en: You've got a cold; you should drink more water.

examples.py: nǐ bù yīng gāi zhè me wǎn shuì jiào
examples.en: You shouldn't go to bed this late.

examples.zh: 他六点下班，现在应该到家了。
examples.py: tā liù diǎn xià bān xiàn zài yīng gāi dào jiā le
examples.en: He finishes work at six; he should be home by now.

rules.rule: 打算 + verb = 'plan to, intend to': more thought-out than 想, less fixed than 要. Time words go before the verb as usual. Negative: 不打算 (don't intend to) or 没打算 (have made no plan to).

examples.zh: 我打算明年去中国留学。
examples.py: wǒ dǎ suàn míng nián qù zhōng guó liú xué
examples.en: I plan to go and study in China next year.

examples.py: zhōu mò nǐ dǎ suàn zuò shén me
examples.en: What are you planning to do at the weekend?

examples.zh: 我们今年不打算买房子。
examples.py: wǒ men jīn nián bù dǎ suàn mǎi fáng zi
examples.en: We don't intend to buy a house this year.

rules.note: 打算 is also a noun: 你有什么打算？ 'What are your plans?'

right.py: fú wù yuán wǒ yào yī bēi kā fēi

contrasts.why: 想 cannot take a noun to mean 'want'. Order with 要 + noun, or add a verb: 我想喝一杯咖啡.

right.py: wǒ hěn xiǎng qù zhōng guó lǚ yóu
right.en: I really want to travel to China.

contrasts.why: 要 does not take 很 or 非常. A wish with a degree adverb is 想 (or 想要).

contrasts.wrong: 你不要给我打电话，发短信就行。

right.zh: 你不用给我打电话，发短信就行。
right.py: nǐ bù yòng gěi wǒ dǎ diàn huà fā duǎn xìn jiù xíng
right.en: You don't need to call me; a text will do.

contrasts.why: 不要 + verb said to someone is a prohibition: 'don't call me'. 'No need to' is 不用.

right.py: míng tiān fàng jià nǐ bù yòng shàng bān
right.en: Tomorrow is a holiday; you don't have to work.

contrasts.why: 得 (děi) has no negative with 不. 'Don't have to' is always 不用.

right.py: wǒ míng tiān bù qù gōng sī
right.en: I'm not going to the office tomorrow.

contrasts.why: 要 for 'going to' is not negated with 不要: 不要去 would be heard as a refusal ('I won't go!'). Say 不 + verb (or 不打算, 不会); 不用去 if the meaning is 'don't have to go'.

right.py: wǒ xiǎng wǒ de jiā rén

contrasts.why: 'Miss' is 想 + person. 要 + person would mean 'want (to have)' them.

right.py: wǒ xiǎng yào yī gè xīn diàn nǎo

contrasts.why: A wished-for thing needs 想要 + noun, or 想 + verb (我想买一个新电脑). Bare 想 + thing does not mean 'want'.

right.py: wǒ jué de tā bù huì tóng yì

contrasts.why: English 'I don't think that...' puts the negative up front; Chinese puts it inside the clause: 我觉得 / 我想 + 他不会.

contrasts.wrong: 从我家到学校想半个小时。

right.zh: 从我家到学校要半个小时。
right.py: cóng wǒ jiā dào xué xiào yào bàn gè xiǎo shí
right.en: It takes half an hour from my home to school.

contrasts.why: 'Takes' + duration is 要 (or 需要 / 得). 想 is only for a person's wish or thought.

cheat: Noun right after it? 要 (ordering, buying) or 想要 (wishing). Never bare 想, unless you mean 'miss'.
很 / 非常 / 有点儿 in front? 想 or 想要, never 要.
想 + person = miss; 想 + clause = think; 想 + verb = would like to.
Negative: don't feel like = 不想; don't! = 不要 / 别; no need = 不用.
得 (děi) = have to. Its negative is 不用, never 不得.
Time word + 要 + verb = going to; 要 + duration or price = takes / costs.
Consent = 愿意; advice = 应该 (不应该 = shouldn't); a plan = 打算.
